newsitem.title: ITALY: Codpiece back in fashion in Westwood's show.
newsitem.headline: Codpiece back in fashion in Westwood's show.

text.p: Briton Vivienne Westwood wrenched men's fashion theatrically back to the 16th century codpiece and hose in her winter collection at the Milan shows.

Diminutive blonde-haired Westwood recreated the Tudor dress of English King Henry VIII, famous for his six wives, by widening the upper body with puffed sleeves on elaborate doublet-style jackets and contrasting these with tights.
"The Renaissance which began in Italy migrated to the rest of Europe in the 16th century and this period is the focus of our collection," Westwood said at the show late on Monday night.

Puffball breeches in slashed red satin stopped at the thigh while Westwood also produced a contour-hugging red and grey sectioned jumpsuit with ties across the hip as well as trousers and pants with unstructured codpiece-style front panels.
Brick red Scots tartan kilts and doublets were embroidered with beads while models wore vibrant red lipstick, gold necklaces and bonnets on their heads.

More wearable designs in the 1997/98 autumn/winter menswear collection included two and three-piece suits worn with wide 1970s-style ties and heeled boots, and tailored grey damask frock coats flared at the hip over trousers in a similar fabric.

Italian design house Fendi, showing its collection in a mosaic-floored palazzo on Milan's exclusive Via Monte Napoleone on Wednesday, stayed firmly in the 20th century with a casual but sophisticated collection of predominantly browns and greys.

The overall silhouette was slender but well-proportioned at the shoulders, with trousers straight and narrow or slightly bagged and gathered at the ankle like golfing pants, and worn over short, zipped boots or loafers.

For men still wanting ties with their jackets there were monochrome and floral prints, but for those following a growing trend towards suits without ties came fine-knit jersey shirts with collars in single tone chocolate brown or grey.
Suits themselves came in two and three pieces in brown or grey with a beigy-pink chalk stripe, brown or mustard yellow corduroy or maroon tweed.
For evening models wore velvet waistcoats in burgundy, simple one-button black velvet jackets and close fitting straight black trousers with a double stripe down the side.
Outdoor wear included generously proportioned panelled fur coats reaching to the calf as well as a selection of leather and suede jackets and simple high-crowned suede and leather caps.
Gucci takes the wraps off its winterwear later on Tuesday and the shows continue until Thursday, when top designer Giorgio Armani closes the five-day event with his collection.
